subtitle: Chocolate masa atole
verso: Champurrado and a tamal: the cold can't hurt us at all!
story: A thick chocolate atole made with masa, sweetened with piloncillo and frothed with a wooden molinillo. It's for cold mornings, posadas and Día de Muertos, with tamales.

ingredients.title: Champurrado
items: ½ cup masa harina (or 4 oz fresh masa)
4 cups water (the traditional way), milk, or half and half
1 tablet (3 oz) Mexican chocolate, chopped (chocolate de metate if you can find it)
3–4 oz piloncillo, grated (or ⅓ cup brown sugar)

steps: Whisk the masa into the warm water until there are no lumps. Strain.
In a pot, simmer the water or milk with the cinnamon, piloncillo, salt and anise for 10 minutes.
Add the chocolate and whisk until melted.
Pour in the masa mixture slowly, whisking constantly.
Simmer on low, stirring constantly, 10 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon. Take out the cinnamon.
Froth with a molinillo, rolling it between your palms, or with a whisk. Serve hot.
pressureNote: No pressure-cooker version. Atole needs constant stirring, and masa scorches under pressure.
tips: Keep stirring. Masa sticks to the bottom and burns fast.

variations.name: Atole Blanco con Canela
variations.subtitle: Cinnamon masa atole
variations.note: The plain atole underneath every flavored one.
steps: Dissolve the masa in [[2 cups]] of the liquid and strain.
Simmer the rest of the liquid with the cinnamon and sugar.
Whisk in the masa and cook, stirring, 10 minutes until thick. Add the vanilla.
